title: ₹10,000, Six Colleagues and No Computer: Infosys Begins in Pune
conflicts: Founding date: 7 July 1981 (Murthy's 2018 oral history, The Week) vs 2 July 1981 (commonly cited incorporation date); story says 'July 1981'. Capital: Murthy says '$250, equivalent to 10,000 rupees' (dollar figure inconsistent with 1981 exchange rates); Sudha says she gave ₹10,000 of ₹10,250; story uses rupees. Loan vs gift vs investment: described differently by outlets; story says 'gave'. Softronics dated 1975-76 (CHM interviewer) or 1977 (HBS); story says 'in the 1970s'. Computer import: about three years and fifty Delhi visits (Murthy) vs over two years (Nilekani); story says about three years and many trips.
notes: Built on Murthy's two Computer History Museum oral histories (2018, 2020) plus Sudha Murty's 2024 remarks and Murthy's 2024 admission that keeping her out of Infosys was 'wrongly idealistic'. Quote complicates: Seneca on how benefits are cheapened once received, set against her funding the company yet being kept out of it. The other four co-founders are not named because no source read here lists them; the Infosys history page blocks automated reading.
